title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 14 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Corinthians chapter 14 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 14 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Corinthians Chapter 14.

questions.question: In 1 Corinthians 14, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: He that prophesieth speaketh unto men
I would that ye all spake with tongues
If the trumpet give an uncertain sound
questions.explanation: The command to follow after charity appears first in 1 Corinthians 14:1.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 14:2, to whom does he that speaketh in an unknown tongue speak?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 14:2 states that he that speaketh in an unknown tongue speaketh not unto men, but unto God.

questions.question: What three purposes does he that prophesieth serve according to 1 Corinthians 14:3?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 14:3 says that he that prophesieth speaketh unto men to edification, and exhortation, and comfort.

questions.question: Who does he that speaketh in an unknown tongue edify according to 1 Corinthians 14:4?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 14:4 states that he that speaketh in an unknown tongue edifieth himself.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 14:5, who is greater, he that prophesieth or he that speaketh with tongues?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 14:5 states that greater is he that prophesieth than he that speaketh with tongues.

questions.question: What must accompany speaking with tongues for the church to receive edifying according to 1 Corinthians 14:5?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 14:5 says except he interpret, that the church may receive edifying.

questions.question: What will Paul profit the brethren if he comes speaking with tongues without revelation, knowledge, prophesying, or doctrine according to 1 Corinthians 14:6?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 14:6 asks what profit is there if Paul speaks with tongues without revelation, knowledge, prophesying, or doctrine, implying no profit.

questions.question: What is the example used in 1 Corinthians 14:7 to illustrate the importance of distinct sounds?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 14:7 uses the example of pipe or harp giving distinction in sounds.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 14:8, what will happen if the trumpet gives an uncertain sound?
options: No one will prepare himself to the battle
questions.correctAnswer: No one will prepare himself to the battle
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 14:8 says if the trumpet give an uncertain sound, who shall prepare himself to the battle?

questions.question: What happens if words spoken by the tongue are not easy to understand according to 1 Corinthians 14:9?
options: It shall be spoken into the air
questions.correctAnswer: It shall be spoken into the air
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 14:9 states that if words are not easy to understand, ye shall speak into the air.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 14:12, what should those zealous of spiritual gifts seek?
options: To excel to the edifying of the church
questions.correctAnswer: To excel to the edifying of the church
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 14:12 instructs those zealous of spiritual gifts to seek that they may excel to the edifying of the church.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Corinthians 14:13, one who speaketh in an unknown tongue should pray to interpret.
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 14:13 says let him that speaketh in an unknown tongue pray that he may interpret.

questions.question: True or False: 1 Corinthians 14:14 states that if one pray in an unknown tongue, their spirit prayeth but their understanding is unfruitful.
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 14:14 explicitly states that if I pray in an unknown tongue, my spirit prayeth but my understanding is unfruitful.

questions.question: True or False: 1 Corinthians 14:11 explains that if one does not understand the meaning of the voice, both the speaker and listener are as barbarians to each other.
questions.explanation: This fact is true but it is taken from 1 Corinthians 14:11 which is allowed for two questions only; this question is the third about that verse, so it is invalid as a false statement here. The actual false statement is below.

questions.question: True or False: 1 Corinthians 14 says that speaking in tongues is always better than prophesying.
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 14:5 says greater is he that prophesieth than he that speaketh with tongues, so the statement is false.

medium.title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 14 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Corinthians Chapter 14 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What does Paul say he will do in 1 Corinthians 14:15?
options: I will pray with the spirit, and I will pray with the understanding also.
I will sing with the spirit, and I will sing with the understanding also.
I will speak in tongues more than you all.
I will teach others with my voice.
questions.correctAnswer: I will pray with the spirit, and I will pray with the understanding also.
questions.explanation: This answer is correct as it directly quotes 1 Corinthians 14:15.

questions.question: What does 1 Corinthians 14:17 indicate about giving thanks in the spirit?
options: It is beneficial for the church.
questions.explanation: This answer is correct as it reflects the message of 1 Corinthians 14:17.

questions.question: What does Paul express in 1 Corinthians 14:18 about speaking in tongues?
options: I thank my God, I speak with tongues more than ye all.
I wish you all spoke in tongues.
Speaking in tongues is less important than prophesying.
Tongues are essential for church unity.
questions.correctAnswer: I thank my God, I speak with tongues more than ye all.
questions.explanation: This is directly quoted from 1 Corinthians 14:18.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 14:19, what does Paul prefer when in the church?
options: To speak five words with understanding.
To prophesy in an unknown tongue.
questions.correctAnswer: To speak five words with understanding.
questions.explanation: This reflects the preference stated in 1 Corinthians 14:19.

questions.question: In 1 Corinthians 14:20, Paul advises the brethren to be what in understanding?
questions.explanation: This is what Paul instructs in 1 Corinthians 14:20.

questions.question: What is the purpose of tongues according to 1 Corinthians 14:22?
options: For a sign to those who believe not.
For the edifying of the church.
questions.correctAnswer: For a sign to those who believe not.
questions.explanation: This is stated in 1 Corinthians 14:22.

questions.question: What happens if the whole church speaks with tongues, according to 1 Corinthians 14:23?
questions.explanation: This reflects the warning given in 1 Corinthians 14:23.

questions.question: What is the outcome for an unbeliever who hears prophesying according to 1 Corinthians 14:24?
questions.explanation: This is the outcome described in 1 Corinthians 14:24.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 14:25, what will happen when the secrets of the heart are revealed?
options: The person will speak in tongues.
questions.explanation: This is stated in 1 Corinthians 14:25.

questions.question: In 1 Corinthians 14:26, what does Paul say should be the focus when coming together?
options: Let all things be done unto edifying.
Let all things be done in silence.
Let all things be done with tongues.
Let all things be done for show.
questions.correctAnswer: Let all things be done unto edifying.
questions.explanation: This reflects the instruction given in 1 Corinthians 14:26.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 14:28, what should someone do if there is no interpreter for their tongue?
options: Let him keep silence in the church.
questions.correctAnswer: Let him keep silence in the church.
questions.explanation: This is the instruction provided in 1 Corinthians 14:28.

questions.question: The church should seek to excel in what, as stated in 1 Corinthians 14:12?
questions.explanation: This is the focus outlined in 1 Corinthians 14:12.

questions.question: It is true that Paul encourages speaking in tongues according to 1 Corinthians 14:5?
questions.explanation: This is true as Paul expresses a desire for all to speak in tongues in 1 Corinthians 14:5.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 14:13, a person speaking in an unknown tongue must pray for what?
questions.explanation: The verse indicates they should pray for interpretation, not just to pray.

questions.question: In 1 Corinthians 14:9, speaking words easy to be understood is emphasized?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 14:9 emphasizes understanding in communication, not just speaking.

hard.title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 14 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Corinthians Chapter 14.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 14:29, how many prophets should speak before the others judge?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 14:29 states, 'Let the prophets speak two or three, and let the other judge.'

questions.question: What should the first prophet do if another sitting nearby receives a revelation, according to 1 Corinthians 14:30?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 14:30 commands that if anything is revealed to another that sits by, the first should hold his peace.

questions.question: In 1 Corinthians 14:31, why may all prophesy one by one?
options: That all may learn and all may be comforted
To show who is the greatest prophet
questions.correctAnswer: That all may learn and all may be comforted
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 14:31 explains that all may prophesy one by one so that all may learn and all may be comforted.

questions.question: What does 1 Corinthians 14:32 teach about the spirits of the prophets?
options: They are subject to the prophets
questions.correctAnswer: They are subject to the prophets
questions.explanation: Verse 32 states, 'And the spirits of the prophets are subject to the prophets,' indicating control by the prophets themselves.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 14:33, what kind of author is God described as?
options: Not the author of confusion, but of peace
The author of confusion and chaos
The author of strict laws only
questions.correctAnswer: Not the author of confusion, but of peace
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 14:33 states, 'For God is not the author of confusion, but of peace, as in all churches of the saints.'

questions.question: What instruction is given to women in the church according to 1 Corinthians 14:34?
options: Let your women keep silence in the churches
Women should teach the children only
Women should speak freely in the church
questions.correctAnswer: Let your women keep silence in the churches
questions.explanation: Verse 34 instructs, 'Let your women keep silence in the churches: for it is not permitted unto them to speak; but they are commanded to be under obedience, as also saith the law.'

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'prophētēs' in 1 Corinthians 14:29 mean?
questions.explanation: The Greek word 'prophētēs' (προφήτης) in 1 Corinthians 14:29 means 'prophet,' referring to one who speaks by divine inspiration.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominent in 1 Corinthians 14:33 where God is described as 'not the author of confusion, but of peace'?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 14:33 uses antithesis by contrasting 'confusion' with 'peace' to emphasize God's nature.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the theme of speaking with other tongues as found in 1 Corinthians 14:21?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 14:21 quotes Isaiah 28:11 regarding speaking with other tongues and lips to this people.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage connects with the orderly conduct in the church as emphasized in 1 Corinthians 14:40?
questions.explanation: 1 Timothy 2:12 discusses order and authority in the church, connecting with 1 Corinthians 14:40’s emphasis on decency and order.

questions.question: What instruction immediately precedes 1 Corinthians 14:29 about prophets speaking two or three?
options: If any man speak in an unknown tongue, let it be by two, or at the most by three
Let all things be done decently and in order
If any man be ignorant, let him be ignorant
questions.correctAnswer: If any man speak in an unknown tongue, let it be by two, or at the most by three
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 14:27 immediately precedes verse 29 and instructs that if anyone speaks in tongues, it should be by two or three at most.

questions.question: What cultural context helps explain Paul's instruction in 1 Corinthians 14:34-35 about women keeping silence in churches?
options: Jewish law and Greco-Roman social norms about women's roles
questions.correctAnswer: Jewish law and Greco-Roman social norms about women's roles
questions.explanation: Paul’s instruction reflects the prevailing Jewish law and Greco-Roman cultural norms that restricted women’s public speech, as cited in 1 Corinthians 14:34.

questions.question: What typology is evident in 1 Corinthians 14:21 where tongues are described as a sign to unbelievers?
options: The use of tongues as a sign fulfills Isaiah’s prophecy of judgment
The tabernacle as a type of the church
The Passover as a type of Christ’s sacrifice
The manna as a type of spiritual nourishment
questions.correctAnswer: The use of tongues as a sign fulfills Isaiah’s prophecy of judgment
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 14:21 typologically fulfills Isaiah 28:11, where speaking in tongues is a sign of judgment to unbelievers.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Corinthians 14:39, believers are encouraged to desire prophecy and forbid speaking in tongues.
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 14:39 instructs believers to 'covet to prophesy, and forbid not to speak with tongues,' so forbidding tongues is not encouraged.

questions.question: True or False: 1 Corinthians 14:40 teaches that all things in the church should be done decently and in order.
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 14:40 clearly states, 'Let all things be done decently and in order,' emphasizing proper order in church practices.

theological.title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 14 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Corinthians Chapter 14 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 Corinthians 14:4 teach about sanctification?
options: Speaking in tongues edifies the individual believer
Prophecy is primarily for personal spiritual growth
Speaking in tongues edifies the entire church
All spiritual gifts equally edify the church
questions.correctAnswer: Speaking in tongues edifies the individual believer
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 14:4 states that he who speaks in an unknown tongue edifies himself, indicating a personal aspect of sanctification.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 Corinthians 14:22 teach about the role of tongues and prophecy in salvation?
options: Tongues are a sign to believers, prophecy to unbelievers
Both tongues and prophecy serve as signs to believers
Tongues are a sign to unbelievers, prophecy to believers
Neither tongues nor prophecy serve as signs in the church
questions.correctAnswer: Tongues are a sign to unbelievers, prophecy to believers
questions.explanation: Verse 22 explains tongues are for a sign to those who believe not, while prophecy serves those who believe, clarifying their distinct salvific roles.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 Corinthians 14:32 teach about the authority and submission of prophetic spirits?
options: Prophetic spirits operate independently of the prophet's control
Prophetic spirits are subject to the prophets themselves
Prophetic spirits override the prophet’s will
Prophetic spirits are unpredictable and uncontrollable
questions.correctAnswer: Prophetic spirits are subject to the prophets themselves
questions.explanation: Verse 32 teaches that the spirits of prophets are under their control, emphasizing human responsibility in prophecy.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 1 Corinthians 14:33 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 14:33 states that God is not the author of confusion but of peace, highlighting His attribute of peace.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 1 Corinthians 14:37 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Verse 37 emphasizes that the things Paul writes are commandments of the Lord, demonstrating God's faithfulness in revealing truth.

questions.question: How does 1 Corinthians 14:19 connect to the theme of effective ministry elsewhere in Scripture?
options: Teaching with understanding is preferred over quantity of words
Speaking in tongues is the highest form of worship
Quantity of spiritual gifts is more important than clarity
Public worship should be silent and contemplative
questions.correctAnswer: Teaching with understanding is preferred over quantity of words
questions.explanation: Verse 19 prioritizes intelligible teaching over many words in tongues, connecting to biblical themes valuing clear instruction (cf. Acts 18:11).

questions.question: How does 1 Corinthians 14:24-25 anticipate the gospel’s power to convict unbelievers?
options: Unbelievers are convinced and worship God through prophetic revelation
Unbelievers remain unaffected by spiritual gifts
Unbelievers only respond to miracles, not prophecy
Unbelievers reject all manifestations of the Spirit
questions.correctAnswer: Unbelievers are convinced and worship God through prophetic revelation
questions.explanation: These verses show prophecy revealing the secrets of the heart, leading unbelievers to conviction and worship, foreshadowing gospel effectiveness.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 13 and 28 teach about the necessity of interpretation in speaking with tongues?
options: Interpretation is optional for personal edification
Interpretation is necessary for the church’s understanding
Interpretation is only required for prophets
Interpretation nullifies the gift of tongues
questions.correctAnswer: Interpretation is necessary for the church’s understanding
questions.explanation: Verse 13 calls for praying for interpretation, and verse 28 mandates silence if none is present, showing interpretation’s necessity for edification.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 5 and 40 teach about orderly worship and the priority of prophecy?
options: Prophecy is superior and worship should be conducted decently and in order
Tongues are superior and disorder is acceptable for spiritual gifts
All gifts are equal and order is secondary to freedom
Worship is spontaneous without any guidelines
questions.correctAnswer: Prophecy is superior and worship should be conducted decently and in order
questions.explanation: Verse 5 shows prophecy’s superiority over tongues without interpretation, and verse 40 commands decency and order, linking doctrine and practice.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 3 and 26 teach about the purpose and practice of prophecy in the church assembly?
options: Prophecy is for personal encouragement and should be done silently
Prophecy edifies, exhorts, comforts, and should be done publicly for building up the church
Prophecy is only for the elders and is not for the assembly
Prophecy is primarily for doctrinal correction
questions.correctAnswer: Prophecy edifies, exhorts, comforts, and should be done publicly for building up the church
questions.explanation: Verse 3 states prophecy edifies, exhorts, and comforts, while verse 26 encourages all to bring gifts including prophecy for edifying, emphasizing public building up.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that 1 Corinthians 14:23-25 endorses chaotic spiritual manifestations that confuse unbelievers. What does 1 Corinthians 14:23-25 actually teach?
options: Unintelligible tongues without interpretation cause unbelievers to think believers are mad
All spiritual gifts cause confusion to unbelievers
Speaking in tongues is the best way to convince unbelievers
questions.correctAnswer: Unintelligible tongues without interpretation cause unbelievers to think believers are mad
questions.explanation: Verse 23 warns that if all speak in tongues without interpretation, unbelievers may think the church members are mad, showing a concern for order and clarity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 Corinthians 14:1 teach about the primacy of love in the pursuit of spiritual gifts?
options: Charity is to be pursued alongside spiritual gifts, with prophecy preferred
Spiritual gifts are more important than love
Love is secondary to the exercise of tongues
Charity and spiritual gifts are unrelated
questions.correctAnswer: Charity is to be pursued alongside spiritual gifts, with prophecy preferred
questions.explanation: Verse 1 commands to follow after charity and desire spiritual gifts, especially to prophesy, linking love and spiritual gifts inseparably.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 1 Corinthians 14:21 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Verse 21 cites God speaking through different tongues and lips yet not being heard, illustrating God's patience and longsuffering toward His people.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 1 Corinthians 14:9 and 14:16 teach about communication and understanding in worship?
options: Unintelligible prayer builds up the church more than understanding
Prayers and blessings must be understood to edify others in worship
Speaking in tongues is the only acceptable form of prayer
Understanding is irrelevant in spiritual expressions
questions.correctAnswer: Prayers and blessings must be understood to edify others in worship
questions.explanation: Verse 9 stresses the need for clear speech to be understood, and verse 16 points out that the unlearned cannot respond 'Amen' if they do not understand, emphasizing edification through understanding.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 Corinthians 14:29 teach about prophetic accountability in the church?
options: Prophets speak without restriction and without judgment
Two or three prophets speak and others judge their words
Prophetic words are accepted without question
Only one prophet should speak in a service
questions.correctAnswer: Two or three prophets speak and others judge their words
questions.explanation: Verse 29 instructs that multiple prophets may speak but others must judge, teaching accountability and discernment in prophecy.
